STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.claim: One dating view holds that the surah is Madinan except verses 52–55, which are Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r1.anchor: Some say it is Madinan except for vv. 52–55, which are Makkan (IK)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.claim: Another dating view holds that the surah is Makkan except verses 19–22, which are Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r2.anchor: others say it is Makkan except for vv.19–22, which are from the Madinan period (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.claim: Most authorities regard the surah as containing both Makkan and Madinan verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r3.anchor: Most say it is a mix of Makkan and Madinan verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.claim: A tradition calls the surah remarkable because it came at night and by day, on journeys and at home, in war and peace, and includes abrogating and abrogated as well as clear and allegorical verses.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r4.anchor: and it has both muḥkam (unambiguous) and mutashābih (symbolic or allegorical) verses (Q)

STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r11.claim: The surah includes significant treatments of Islam's relation to other religions and the Muslim community's place in history.
STUDYQURAN:22:intro/r11.anchor: the relationship of Islam to other religions and the place of the Muslim community in history (vv. 17, 34, 67, 78)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p165/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p165/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p165/r7.claim: The disbelievers' respite reflects God's haste in mercy and deferral of torment; the Prophet should leave their matter to God, who will judge them in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p165/r7.anchor: God shows haste in mercy and defers torment. The Prophet (sws) is directed to consign their matter to God.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r1.claim: These readers use kasra on the sīn in mansik at both occurrences.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r1.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي، (منسكا) بكسر السين في الحرفين جميعا.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r2.claim: The other readers use fatḥa on the sīn in both occurrences.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: منسكا بفتح السين في الحرفين جميعا .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r3.claim: Fatḥa is preferable because the word is either a verbal noun or place noun, and both normally have fatḥa for this verb pattern.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: الفتح أولى لأنه لا يخلو من أن يكون مصدرا أو مكانا، وكلاهما مفتوح العين

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r4.claim: Kasra could mark an exceptional place noun on the mafʿil pattern, as in maṭliʿ and masjid, but that requires transmitted evidence.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r4.anchor: ووجه الكسر: أنه قد يجيء اسم المكان على المفعل من هذا النحو، نحو: المطلع، وإنما هو من طلع يطلع، والمسجد وهو من يسجد

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī may have heard this exceptional place-noun form from native usage.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p277/r5.anchor: فيمكن أن يكون هذا مما شذ أيضا عن قياس الجمهور، فجاء اسم المكان على غير القياس، ولا يقدم على هذا إلا بالسمع، ولعل الكسائي سمع ذلك.

JISHUMI:v7p4955/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4955/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v7p4955/r5.claim: They read mansak with a kasra on the sīn in both occurrences as a noun meaning a slaughter place or place of offering.
JISHUMI:v7p4955/r5.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: منسكا بكسر السين في الحرفين على معنى الاسم، كالمجلس والمطلع، أي: مذبحا،

JISHUMI:v7p4955/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4955/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4955/r6.claim: The other readers use a fatḥa on the sīn in both occurrences as a verbal noun for shedding blood and slaughtering offerings.
JISHUMI:v7p4955/r6.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح السين فيهما على المصدر، مثل: المدخل والمخرج، أي: إراقة الدماء وذبح القرابين.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p374/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p374/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p374/r2.claim: Qatada says the appointed rite is pilgrimage and sacrifice.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p374/r2.anchor: نا سعيد عن قتادة قال: أي حجا وذبحا.

BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r1.claim: A Persian couplet portrays the earth as God’s table, with friend and foe sharing its bounty.
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r1.anchor: اديم زمين سفرة عام أوست برين خوان يغماه دشمن ه دوست

BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r2.claim: Each bodily member has a specific obedience; misusing it exposes a person to divine anger, as the Bustān poems warn against misusing tools, speech, hearing, and sight.
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r2.anchor: ولكل عضو من أعضاء الإنسان طاعة تخصه فإذا لم يصرفه إلى مصارفه ولم يستخدمه فيما يناسب

BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r3.claim: The sign of a person turning to God is to use the heart for reflection on God and the afterlife, the tongue for remembrance and gratitude, and the body for service until death.
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r3.anchor: يقال : علامة المنيب أي المقبل إلى الله تعالى في ثلاث خصال

BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r4.claim: Bursevī asks God to grant steadfast obedience and service and to honor the supplicants with Paradise and union.
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r4.anchor: نسأل الله سبحانه أن يوفقنا لطاعته

BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r5.claim: Every umma means a community, among past and future nations, to whom a messenger was sent.
BURSEVI:v6p40#2/r5.anchor: {لكل أمة} معينة من الأمم الماضية والباقية والأمة جماعة أرسل إليهم رسول

BURSEVI:v6p41/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p41/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p41/r1.claim: Mansak derives from worship and here means a particular religious law; God appointed a distinct law for each community, with no independent or shared transfer between communities.
BURSEVI:v6p41/r1.anchor: مصدر مأخوذ من النسك وهو العبادة أي شريعة خاصة لا لأمة منهم على معنى عينا كل شريعة لأمة معينة

BURSEVI:v6p41/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p41/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p41/r2.claim: The clause “they perform it” reinforces exclusivity; the pronoun refers to each particular community, which alone acts according to its assigned law.
BURSEVI:v6p41/r2.anchor: صفة لمنسكا مؤكدة للقصر المستفاد من تقديم الجار والمجرور على الفعل والضمير لكل أمة باعتبار خصوصها

BURSEVI:v6p41/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p41/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p41/r3.claim: From Moses to Jesus the Torah was the law, from Jesus to the Prophet the Gospel, and for the community from Muḥammad’s mission until Judgment the Qurʾān alone.
BURSEVI:v6p41/r3.anchor: من مبعث موسى إلى مبعث عيسى عليهما السلام ، منسكهم التوراة هم ناسكوها

BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r1.claim: Nizāʿ means pulling something from its place and hence disputing; people of other religions contemporary with the Prophet are addressed.
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r1.anchor: أي : من يعاصرك من أهل الملل يقال : نزع الشيء جذبه من مقره

BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r2.claim: The dispute concerns religion: other groups claim their inherited Torah or Gospel, but those laws belonged to earlier communities before abrogation; the present community has the Qurʾān alone.
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r2.anchor: {فى الامر} أي : في أمر الدين زعما منهم أن شريعتهم ماعين لآبائهم الأولين

BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r3.claim: Bursevī’s Persian gloss emphasizes that no religious dispute is conceivable because the Prophet’s path is clearer than the sun.
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r3.anchor: س بايدكه نزاع نكنند سائر أرباب اديان باتو دركار دين

BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r4.claim: The Prophet is to invite all people without excluding any community, calling them to God’s oneness and worship as laid out in their law.
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r4.anchor: {وادع} الناس كافة ولا تخص أمة دون أمة بالدعوة

BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r5.claim: Straight guidance is the even path that leads to truth: the religion.
BURSEVI:v6p41#2/r5.anchor: أي : طريق موصل إلى الحق سوي وهو الدين

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r1.claim: After describing God’s mercy toward people despite their ingratitude, the passage turns to His favor in prescribing religious duties.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r1.anchor: إعلم أنه تعالى لما قدم ذكر نعمه وبين أنه رؤوف رحيم بعباده

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r2.claim: The verse lacks an initial conjunction because this statement is not attached to what preceded it.

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas takes a manسك as a festival at which the community slaughters an animal.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس عيد ( ا ) يذبحون فيه

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r4.claim: Mujahid interprets the term as a sacrificial offering and says it is specifically used for slaughter.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r4.anchor: ولفظ المنسك مختص بالذبائح عن مجاهد

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r5.speaker: قول ثالث
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r5.claim: A third view understands the term as a familiar place or time appointed for acts of worship.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r5.anchor: مألفا يألفونه إما مكانا معينا أو زمانا معينا لأداء الطاعات

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r6.claim: Rāzī prefers the view attributed to Ibn Abbas through ʿAṭāʾ and chosen by al-Qaffāl: manسك means a religious law or path, since worship is not limited to sacrifice.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r6.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء واختيار القفال وهو الأقرب لقوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r7.claim: He derives manسك from worship; since the name can cover every act of worship, restricting it to sacrifice lacks justification.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r7.anchor: إذا وقع الإسم على كل عبادة فلا وجه للتخصيص

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r8.claim: Against restricting manسك to slaughter by customary usage, Rāzī notes that all the rites of pilgrimage are called manāsik, as in the Prophet’s instruction to learn them from him.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r8.anchor: أن سائر ما يفعل في الحج يوصف بأنه مناسك

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r9.claim: The phrase “they practice it” fits worship better than a specific place or time, answering the proposed place-and-time interpretation.

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r10.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r10.claim: Some restrict the communities meant to Jews and Christians who adhered to a revealed law in Muhammad’s lifetime.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r10.anchor: زعم قوم أن المراد من قوله

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r11.claim: Rāzī allows the verse to include worshippers from every nation, whether their religious traces still remain or not; “they practice it” describes the communities without requiring present worship.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r11.anchor: ولا يمتنع أن يريد كل من تعبد من الأمم سواء بقيت آثارهم أو لم تبق

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r12.claim: A reading of the phrase is understood as commanding Muhammad to remain steadfast in his religion so opponents cannot entice him away.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r12.anchor: أي أثبت في دينك ثباتا لا يطمعون أن يخدعوك

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r13.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r13.claim: Al-Zajjāj reads the prohibition as addressed to the opponents: they must not contend with Muhammad, like the idiom “do not fight him.”
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r13.anchor: قول الزجاج : أنه نهى لهم عن منازعتهم

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r14.claim: Another explanation requires the communities to follow Muhammad and abandon opposition, since his law has become established and supersedes earlier laws; surviving adherents must convert.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r14.anchor: أن المراد أن عليهم اتباعك وترك مخالفتك

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r15.claim: Muhammad is to call every nation, without excluding any, to his law because all are included among those he addresses.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r15.anchor: أي لا تخص بالدعاء أمة دون أمة فكلهم أمتك فادعهم إلى شريعتك

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r16.claim: Guidance could mean the religion itself or its proofs; Rāzī prefers the proofs, a clear path by which the religion is demonstrated.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r16.anchor: والهدى يحتمل نفس الدين ويحتمل أدلة الدين

RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r17.claim: If opponents leave examination of the proofs for disputation and appeals to custom, Muhammad has made his case; warning them that God knows their deeds is then appropriate.
RAZI-FULL:v23p56#2/r17.anchor: فإن عدلوا عن النظر في هذه الأدلة إلى طريقة المراء والتمسك بالعادة فقد بينت وأظهرت ما يلزمك

STUDYQURAN:22:67/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:67/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:22:67/r1.claim: Mansak, rendered rite, can denote either a ritual act or a place of ritual significance.
STUDYQURAN:22:67/r1.anchor: can mean both a ritual act and a place of ritual significance

STUDYQURAN:22:67/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:67/r2.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:22:67/r2.claim: One interpretation advises the Prophet and, by extension, believers not to debate members of other communities about these questions.
STUDYQURAN:22:67/r2.anchor: Let them not argue with thee is understood to mean that the Prophet, and by extension all believers, should not engage in debate

STUDYQURAN:22:67/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:22:67/r3.speaker: some commentators (R)
STUDYQURAN:22:67/r3.claim: An alternative interpretation tells disputants to stop arguing with Muslims and embrace Islam.
STUDYQURAN:22:67/r3.anchor: although some understand this to mean that those who would argue with the Muslims should themselves stop their dispute and embrace Islam (R).

TAB-FULL:v16p625/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r3.claim: For each past community God appointed a customary place for worship and observance of His duties, along with a practice they were to maintain.
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r3.anchor: وقوله: {لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا} [الحج: 67] يقول: لكل جماعة قوم هي خلت من قبلك، جعلنا مألفا يألفونه، ومكانا يعتادونه لعبادتي فيه،

TAB-FULL:v16p625/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r4.claim: The basic Arabic sense of mansak is a place one regularly frequents and becomes accustomed to, for good or evil; Hajj rites take the name because people repeatedly visit their sites for Hajj and ʿUmra.
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r4.anchor: وأصل المنسك في كلام العرب الموضع المعتاد الذي يعتاده الرجل ويألفه لخير أو شر؛

TAB-FULL:v16p625/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r5.claim: The forms minsk (kasra on sīn, fatḥa on mīm) and mansak (fatḥa on both) are dialect forms of the Hijaz and Asad respectively; both were read.
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r5.anchor: وفيه لغتان: (منسك) : بكسر السين وفتح الميم، وذلك من لغة أهل الحجاز، و: (منسك) : بفتح الميم والسين جميعا،

TAB-FULL:v16p625/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the appointed mansak as a festival they customarily observe.
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " قوله: {لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا هم ناسكوه} [الحج: 67] يقول: عيدا "

TAB-FULL:v16p625/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r7.claim: Mujahid describes the mansak as the shedding of sacrificial blood in Mecca, including the blood of sacrificial offerings.
TAB-FULL:v16p625/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا هم ناسكوه} [الحج: 67] قال: «إراقة الدم بمكة»

TAB-FULL:v16p627/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p627/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p627/r1.claim: Qatada glosses mansak as slaughter and Hajj.

TAB-FULL:v16p627/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p627/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p627/r2.claim: Al-Tabari prefers slaughtering sacrificial animals at Mina on the Nahr days: that was the ritual over which polytheists disputed with the Prophet; other livestock slaughter mentioned in al-Anʿām was not a rite, whereas sacrificial offerings are.
TAB-FULL:v16p627/r2.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أن يقال: عني بذلك إراقة الدم أيام النحر بمنى؛ لأن المناسك التي كان المشركون جادلوا فيها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v16p628/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p628/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p628/r1.claim: Al-Tabari applies the command to slaughter and meat, explaining the polytheists’ challenge about eating what people slaughter rather than carrion; Qatada glosses it as not avoiding one’s meat.
TAB-FULL:v16p628/r1.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة: " {فلا ينازعنك في الأمر} [الحج: 67] فلا تتحام لحمك "

TAB-FULL:v16p628/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p628/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p628/r2.claim: Mujahid says the matter in which they must not dispute is slaughter.
TAB-FULL:v16p628/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد: " {فلا ينازعنك في الأمر} [الحج: 67] قال: الذبح "

TAB-FULL:v16p628/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p628/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p628/r3.claim: Qatada explains the command as not avoiding the meat one has slaughtered.
TAB-FULL:v16p628/r3.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة: " {فلا ينازعنك في الأمر} [الحج: 67] فلا تتحام لحمك "

TAB-FULL:v16p628#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p628#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p628#2/r1.claim: Muhammad should call the disputing polytheists to obey God’s order for ritual slaughter; this rite, prescribed for him and his community, is the straight path.
TAB-FULL:v16p628#2/r1.anchor: طريق مستقيم غير زائل عن محجة الحق، والصواب في نسكك الذي جعله لك ولأمتك ربك،

TABATABAI:22:67-68/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r1.claim: The passage closes the sūra's call to preach by exposing shirk, summarizing the believers' duties as worship and good works, and commanding striving in God's cause.
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r1.anchor: بيان الآيات تأمره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بالدعوة وتبين أمورا

TABATABAI:22:67-68/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r2.claim: Mansak is a verbal noun meaning worship, as confirmed by “they perform it”; it is not a place noun, contrary to another proposed explanation.
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r2.anchor: المنسك مصدر ميمي بمعنى النسك وهو العبادة

TABATABAI:22:67-68/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r3.claim: “Each community” means successive past communities through the present one, not different peoples living together in the Prophet's time, because prophecy and its law are universal and one.
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r3.anchor: والمراد بكل أمة هي الأمة بعد الأمة من الأمم الماضين حتى تنتهي إلى هذه الأمة

TABATABAI:22:67-68/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r4.claim: God replaced earlier rites with better ones for later communities as their intellectual development and readiness advanced, so earlier rites were abrogated for successors and cannot invalidate the Prophet's rite.
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r4.anchor: بدل منسك السابقين مما هو أحسن منه في حق اللاحقين لتقدمهم في الرقي الفكري

TABATABAI:22:67-68/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r5.claim: The prohibition addresses unbelievers disputing the Prophet's rites; although they deny his authority, it is not empty, because the verse's opening gives the argument on which it rests.
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r5.anchor: لكن هذا النهي لما كان معتمدا على الحجة لم يصر لغوا لا أثر له وهي صدر الآية

TABATABAI:22:67-68/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r6.claim: The implied objection is that unfamiliar Islamic rites were absent from earlier laws and thus could not be prophetic; the answer is that each community had a distinct rite, later laws superseding earlier ones.
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r6.anchor: كأن الكفار من أهل الكتاب أو المشركين لما رأوا من عبادات الإسلام ما لا عهد لهم به

TABATABAI:22:67-68/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r7.claim: After telling the Prophet not to heed their contention, God turns him back to his task: call people to his Lord.
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r7.anchor: طب نفسا ولا تعبأ بمنازعتهم واشتغل بما أمرت به وهو الدعوة إلى ربك

TABATABAI:22:67-68/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r8.claim: Calling guidance “straight” is a rational metaphor, since straightness properly describes the path toward which guidance leads.
TABATABAI:22:67-68/r8.anchor: وتوصيف الهدي بالاستقامة وهي وصف الصراط الذي إليه الهداية من المجاز العقلي

TABRISI:22:66-70/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:66-70/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:22:66-70/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says each community or past generation was given a religious law that its people practice.
TABRISI:22:66-70/r4.anchor: أي شريعة هم عاملون بها عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:22:66-70/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:66-70/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:66-70/r5.claim: Other explanations take mansak as a familiar worship place or place of worship, including the pilgrimage sites.

TABRISI:22:66-70/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:66-70/r6.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
TABRISI:22:66-70/r6.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda explain mansak as a place for sacrifice, whether at Mina or elsewhere.
TABRISI:22:66-70/r6.anchor: وقيل: موضع قربان أي متعبد في إراقة الدماء مني أو غيره عن مجاهد وقتادة

TABRISI:22:66-70/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:66-70/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:66-70/r7.claim: The command is explained either as forbidding the opponents to dispute with the Prophet, or as addressed to him because a dispute is mutual.
TABRISI:22:66-70/r7.anchor: هذا نهي لهم عن منازعة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. وقيل: نهي له لأن المنازعة تكون من اثنين

TABRISI:22:66-70/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:66-70/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:66-70/r8.claim: Their dispute concerned why Muslims eat animals they slaughter but refuse animals God “killed,” meaning carrion; the instruction is not to quarrel over slaughter.
TABRISI:22:66-70/r8.anchor: ومنازعتهم قولهم أتأكلون ما قتلتم ولا تأكلون ما قتله الله يعنون الميتة أي فلا يخاصمنك في أمر الذبح

TABRISI:22:66-70/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:66-70/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:66-70/r9.claim: Another explanation is that opponents have no right to contest the Prophet’s law, which has abrogated the earlier laws.
TABRISI:22:66-70/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه ليس لهم أن ينازعوك في شريعتهم وقد نسخت هذه الشريعة الشرائع المتقدمة

TABRISI:22:66-70/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:66-70/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:66-70/r10.claim: The Prophet should disregard their quarrelling and call people to God’s oneness and religion.
TABRISI:22:66-70/r10.anchor: أي لا تلتفت إلى منازعتك وادع إلى توحيد ربك وإلى دينه

TABRISI:22:66-70/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:22:66-70/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:22:66-70/r11.claim: Being on straight guidance means following an upright religion.
TABRISI:22:66-70/r11.anchor: إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم } أي على دين قيم

THALABI:v7p32#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p32#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p32#2/r5.claim: A mansak is a customary, regularly visited place for worship; in Arabic it can be a place one frequents for good or bad, and pilgrimage rites are so named because people repeatedly visit their sites.
THALABI:v7p32#2/r5.anchor: لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا مألفا يألفونه وموضعا يعتادونه لعبادة الله،

THALABI:v7p32#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p32#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p32#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains a community's mansak as its festival.
THALABI:v7p32#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا أي عيدا

THALABI:v7p32#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p32#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
THALABI:v7p32#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid and Qatādah take mansak to mean a place where offerings are sacrificed.
THALABI:v7p32#2/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة: موضع قربان يذبحون فيه

THALABI:v7p32#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p32#2/r8.speaker: غيرهم
THALABI:v7p32#2/r8.claim: Other commentators understand mansak to encompass all acts of worship.

THALABI:v7p32#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p32#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p32#2/r9.claim: The command not to dispute concerns the matter of slaughter.
THALABI:v7p32#2/r9.anchor: فلا ينازعنك في الأمر أي في أمر الذبح

THALABI:v7p32#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p32#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p32#2/r10.claim: The verse was revealed about Badīl ibn Warqāʾ, Bishr ibn Sufyān, and Yazīd ibn al-Khunays, who challenged the Muslims for eating what they killed but not what God killed.
THALABI:v7p32#2/r10.anchor: نزلت في بديل بن ورقاء وبشر بن سفيان ويزيد بن الخنيس قالوا لأصحاب رسول الله

THALABI:v7p32#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p32#2/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p32#2/r11.claim: The Prophet is told to invite people to his Lord's religion.
THALABI:v7p32#2/r11.anchor: وادع إلى ربك دين ربك إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r1.claim: Every umma here is a generation that has passed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r2.claim: A manasak is a religious law practiced by that community.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد شريعة هم عاملون بها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r3.speaker: مقاتل وغيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r3.claim: A manasak is an animal sacrifice offered at their festival.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل وغيره: يعني ذبيحة في عيدهم هم ذابحوه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r4.claim: The manasak has already been discussed earlier in this sura.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r4.anchor: تقدم الكلام فيه في هذه السورة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r5.claim: The matter in which they must not dispute is animal sacrifice.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r6.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r6.claim: The verse concerned Badīl ibn Warqāʾ, Bishr ibn Sufyān, Yazīd ibn Khunays, and others who argued that animals killed by God were more deserving to eat than animals Muslims killed with knives.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r6.anchor: قال الكلبي ومقاتل: نزلت في بديل بن ورقاء الخزاعي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r7.claim: The command means that the Prophet must not argue with them, as the following challenge shows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r7.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: معنى قوله {فلا ينازعنك} لا تنازعهم ولا تجادلهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r9.claim: Although they had argued, the reciprocal verb expresses a command not to argue with them; this construction works for mutual debate, unlike a one-way verb such as striking.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p489/r9.anchor: لا يخاصمنك فلان في هذا أبدا، أي: لا تخاصمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r1.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r1.claim: Calling to the Lord means calling people to know Him through monotheism.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل بن سليمان: يعني إلى معرفة ربك وهو التوحيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r2.claim: The call is to uphold the ordinances of the pure monotheistic religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يريد قم بشرائع الحنيفية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r3.claim: Taken together, the command is to call to faith in God and practice the law He prescribed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r3.anchor: والمعنى على هذا: ادع إلى الإيمان به وإعمال ما شرع من الشريعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r4.claim: The straight guidance is the religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r4.anchor: قوله: {إنك لعلى هدى} دين {مستقيم} وهو قال ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r5.claim: No religion created is more upright, excellent, or beloved to God than this one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p491/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يخلق دينا أقوم ولا أفضل منه ولا أحب إلى الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:67-68/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:67-68/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:67-68/r1.claim: Every community has a religious law that its people follow.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:67-68/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:67-68/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:67-68/r2.claim: The verse concerns people who disputed with believers, asking why they ate animals they slaughtered but not those God caused to die.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:22:67-68/r2.anchor: نزلت في الذين جادلوا المؤمنين فقالوا: ما لكم تأكلون ما تقتلون، ولا تأكلون مما قتله الله؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r4.claim: Qatāda says each community was given a pilgrimage and sacrifice rite.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r4.anchor: قوله: {لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا} [الحج: 67] حجا وذبحا في تفسير قتادة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r5.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r5.claim: Mujāhid glosses performing the rite as the shedding of blood.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r6.claim: Yahya clarifies that the word means the sacrificial rite.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r7.claim: Polytheists must not turn the Prophet away from his religion; Yahya says this is addressed to the Prophet.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r7.anchor: {فلا ينازعنك في الأمر} [الحج: 67] أي لا يحولنك المشركون عن هذا الدين الذي أنت عليه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r8.claim: Calling to the Lord means calling to worship Him sincerely.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r8.anchor: {وادع إلى ربك} [الحج: 67] أي إلى الإخلاص له.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r9.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying he was commanded to fight people until they profess God's oneness; then blood and property are protected except by right, and their account is with God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p387/r9.anchor: عثمان، عن نعيم بن عبد الله، عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أمرت أن أقاتل الناس حتى يقولوا لا إله إلا الله فإذا قالوها عصموا بها دماءهم وأموالهم إلا بحقها وحسابهم على الله» .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p388/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p388/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p388/r1.claim: The straight guidance is Islam, which keeps a person upright until it brings them to Paradise.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p388/r1.anchor: قوله: {إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم} [الحج: 67] يعني على دين مستقيم، الإسلام تستقيم به حتى يهجم بك على الجنة.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r1.claim: Mensek can mean sacrifice, a place or procedure for sacrifice, a place or form of worship, or religion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r1.anchor: mensek kelimesi “kurban kesme ibadeti, kurban kesme yeri veya kurban kesme usulü” mânalarına geldiği gibi, “ibadet mahalli, ibadet şekli ve din” anlamında da kullanılır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r2.claim: Verse 34's context led many exegetes to connect the term with sacrifice, though this verse has drawn several readings.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r2.anchor: 34. âyetin bağlamı genel olarak müfessirleri bu kelimeyi kurban kesme ibadeti ile irtibatlandırmaya yöneltmiş olmakla beraber, bu âyette birbirinden farklı yorumlar yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r3.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r3.claim: Tabari records one interpretation as the festival each community celebrates.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r4.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r4.claim: Tabari records an interpretation referring to the blood each community sheds.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r5.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r5.claim: Tabari records an interpretation referring to the sacrifice each community offers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r5.anchor: Taberî, “kutladıkları bayram, akıttıkları kan, kestikleri kurban

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r6.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r6.claim: Tabari records an interpretation referring to each community's Hajj ritual.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r6.anchor: Taberî, “kutladıkları bayram, akıttıkları kan, kestikleri kurban ve hac ibadeti”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r7.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r7.claim: Tabari prefers the blood sacrifice at Mina on the Eid days, because the dispute between the Prophet and the polytheists concerned this matter.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r7.anchor: Taberî, “kutladıkları bayram, akıttıkları kan, kestikleri kurban ve hac ibadeti” şeklindeki yorumları aktardıktan sonra, kendisinin burada kurban bayramı günlerinde Mina’da akıtılan kanın kastedildiği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r8.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r8.claim: Ibn Ashur reads the term as a place of worship and argues that shared worship space across revealed religions rebuts polytheists' separate temples and altars for idols.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r8.anchor: İbn Âşûr, kelimenin “ibadet mahalli” anlamından yola çıkarak bu ifadenin karşı görüşleri geçersiz kılan bir delil taşıdığını ileri sürer

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r9.claim: The author distinguishes the term's sense in verse 34, a place of sacrifice, from its sense here, the Hajj site.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r9.anchor: Şu var ki mensek kelimesiyle 34. âyette “kurban yeri”, burada ise “hac mahalli” kastedilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r10.claim: Razi and Shawkani understand mensek as religion or religious rules because the context does not require a narrower sense; the author adopts that meaning in the translation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r10.anchor: Râzî (XXIII, 64) ve Şevkânî (III, 526-527) gibi müfessirler ise âyetin bağlamı bir anlam sınırlandırmasını gerektirmediği için kelimeyi din

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r11.speaker: rivayetler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r11.claim: Some reports connect the verse's revelation to an objection that polytheists prohibited animals that died naturally while permitting animals they slaughtered themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r11.anchor: Bazı rivayetlerde bu âyetin müşriklerin kendiliğinden ölmüş (meyte = murdar) hayvan etinin yasaklanması hükmüne işaretle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r12.claim: Every community received religious rulings suited to its circumstances and human development; recognizing this should keep Meccan polytheists from finding Muhammad's prophethood strange.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r12.anchor: öncelikle Allah tarafından toplumların şartlarına ve beşerî gelişmelere göre farklı dinî hükümlerin bildirilmiş olduğu realitesine dikkat çekilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r13.claim: The remaining issue is whether Muhammad's message has a sound source and calls to the right path; the verse directs him to continue calling his Lord's way and affirms his straight guidance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:22:67/r13.anchor: geriye onun getirdiği mesajın sahih bir kaynağa dayanıp dayanmadığı ve doğru yola çağrıda bulunup bulunmadığı meselesi kalır

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r1.claim: God is worthy of praise whether or not He gives: giving merits praise as gratitude, while withholding merits praise as commendation.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r1.anchor: الغني الحميد المستحق للحمد : أعطى أو لم يعط ؛ فإن أعطى استحق الحمد الذي هو الشكر

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r2.claim: Whatever creatures can use and are enabled to enjoy is as if subjected to them; licit use by permission, invitation, and command is grace, while its opposite is a trap and gradual ruin.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r2.anchor: فمن استمتع بشىء على وجه الإباحة والإذن والدعاء إليه والأمر به فذلك إنعام وإكرام ، ومن كان بالعكس فمكر

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r3.claim: God's inspiration of shipbuilding and its uses, including riding, carrying cargo, crossing long distances, and reaching far places, is great kindness and blessing.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r3.anchor: إلهام العبد بصنعها ووجوه الانتفاع بها ؛ بالحمل فيها وركوبها فمن أعظم إحسان الله وإرفاقه بالعبد

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r4.claim: The stable earth, sky that does not fall, and stars that guide in darkness and adorn the heavens are proofs that bring certainty and peace of heart.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r4.anchor: جعل الأرض قرارا للخلق من غير أن تميد ، وجعل السماء بناء من غير وقوع ، وجعل فيها من الكواكب

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r5.claim: Human deaths and revivals are limited, but the spiritual reviving and deadening of worshippers' times is uncountable; the poem likens remembrance to dying and coming alive.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r5.anchor: إحياء النفوس وإماتتها مرات محصورة ، وإحياء أوقات العباد وإماتتها لا حصر له ولا عد

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r6.claim: For ordinary people, hopes revive through witnessing God's favor and die when they see His inviolable might; the spiritually excellent have enduring life and renewal.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r6.anchor: يحيي الآمال بإشهاد تفضله ، ثم يميتها بالإطلاع على تعززه . ويقال هذه صفة العوام منهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r7.claim: God's existence suffices as a substitute for everything that is lost.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r7.anchor: وأنى يحيا غيره وفي وجوده - سبحانه - غنية وخلف عن كل فائت

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r8.claim: God assigns every community a rite to follow and every group a path to tread.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r8.anchor: جعل لكل فريق شرعة هم واردوها ، ولكل جماعة طريقة هم سالكوها

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r9.claim: Each spiritual station has its own inhabitants: worship, striving, gnosis, and love each have their fitting practitioners.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r9.anchor: فبساط التعبد موطوء بأقدام العابدين ، ومشاهد الاجتهاد معمورة بأصحاب التكلف من المجتهدين

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r10.claim: The Prophet should witness the turns of destiny, do what duty requires, and stop at the spiritual resources permitted to him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r10.anchor: اشهد تصاريف الأقدار ، واعمل بموجب التكليف ، وانته دون ما أذنت له من المناهل

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r11.claim: Leave disputants to God and do not rely on clever stratagems or seek support from one's peers, who are empty forms without meaning.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r11.anchor: كلهم إلينا عندما راموا من الجدال ، ولا تتكل على ماتختاره من الاحتيال ، واحذر جنوح قلبك إلى الاستعانة بالأمثال

QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r12.claim: For outsiders, the author invokes the verse saying that a person will suffice as his own reckoner on the Day of Resurrection.
QUSHAYRI:v2p329/r12.anchor: أما الأجانب فيقول لهم : { كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا }

DAMGHANI:v1p472/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r6.claim: Hudā can mean the religion of Islam.
DAMGHANI:v1p472/r6.anchor: الثاني الهدى دين الإسلام قوله تعالى في سورة الحج وإنك لعلى هدى وقوله تعالى في سورة البقرة قل إن هدى الله هوالهدى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses hudā as guidance and guidance as clarification.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة الهدى : الإرشاد ، والإرشاد : البيان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the root sense of hudā in Arabic is divine enabling or success.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن الأنباري : أصل الهدى في كلام العرب : التوفيق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r3.claim: Some scholars connect hadiyya, a gift, with guiding or correcting affection; hawādī are the foremost visible necks of a troop of horses.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r3.anchor: وذكر بعض أهل العلم : أن الهدية سميت هدية لأنها تدل على تقويم الوداد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r4.claim: The lexical entry also uses hudā for leading the bridal procession, sacrificial livestock sent to the sanctuary, and walking between two people for support.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p625#2/r4.anchor: وتقول : أقبلت هوادي الخيل ، إذا بدت أعناقها

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p294#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p294#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p294#6/r1.claim: Mansakan means a festival or feast day.

SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r1.claim: هم ناسكوه is an adjective clause describing منسكا; منسك has previously been read with fatḥa or kasra and analyzed as either a verbal noun or a place.
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r1.anchor: قوله: { هم ناسكوه }: هذه الجملة صفة ل منسكا. وقد تقدم أنه يقرأ بالفتح والكسر.

SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya argues ناسكوه implies that منسك is a verbal noun, since a place would take ناسكون فيه.
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " ناسكوه يعطي أن المنسك المصدر، ولو كان مكانا لقال: ناسكون فيه "

SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r3.claim: The author says this does not prove a verbal noun: an adverb of place can be extended to behave like a direct object and take the verb's pronoun without في.
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r3.anchor: وما قاله غير لازم؛ لأنه قد يتسع في الظرف فيجري مجرى المفعول به،

SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r4.claim: Poetry demonstrates extension of a time adverb as a direct object in يوم شهدناه; the cited poet is unnamed.
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r4.anchor: ومن الاتساع في ظرف الزمان قوله: 3398 ويوم شهدناه سليمى وعامرا قليل سوى الطعن النهال نوافله

SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r5.claim: An anonymous poetic example uses a place adverb as a direct object in مشرب أشربه, meaning أشرب فيه.
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r5.anchor: ومن الاتساع في ظرف المكان قوله: 3399 ومشرب أشربه وشيل لا أجن الطعم ولا وبيل

SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r6.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r6.claim: A reading has the light nūn in ينازعنك.
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r6.anchor: قوله: { فلا ينازعنك } وقرىء بالنون الخفيفة.

SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r7.speaker: أبو مجلز
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r7.claim: Abū Majlaz reads فلا ينزعنك, from removing or pulling something away.
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز: " فلا ينزعنك " من كذا أي: قلعته منه.

SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r8.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives ينازعنك from mutual disputation where one party overcomes the other.
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r8.anchor: وقال الزجاج: " هو من نازعته فنزعته أنزعه أي: غلبته في المنازعة ".

SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r9.claim: The prohibition resembles فلا يصدنك عنها; this verse introduces لكل أمة without a coordinating wāw, unlike its earlier counterpart.
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r9.anchor: ومجيء هذه الآية كقوله تعالى: { فلا يصدنك عنها } وقولهم: لا أرينك ههنا.

SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that the earlier لكل أمة is coordinated because it sits among related verses on sacrificial rites, while this occurrence is surrounded by less related material.
SAMIN-DURR:22:67/r10.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " لأن " تلك " وقعت مع ما يدانيها ويناسبها من الآي الواردة في أمر النسائك،

ZAJJAJ:v3p436/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p436/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p436/r4.claim: Zajjaj says he has already explained the word منسكا earlier.
ZAJJAJ:v3p436/r4.anchor: ومنسكا، وقد تقدم الشرح في هذا.

ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r1.claim: The command means do not argue or dispute with them; the following instruction for the case that they argue supports this sense.
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r1.anchor: لا يجادلنك فيه، ومعناه لا تنازعهم

ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r2.claim: This injunction precedes fighting, as indicated by the following direction about what to say if they argue.
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r2.anchor: وإن جادلوك فقل الله أعلم بما تعملون

ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r3.claim: Though they had already argued, the prohibition addresses the Prophet, telling him not to enter into a dispute with them.
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r3.anchor: فالمعنى أنه نهي له - صلى الله عليه وسلم - عن

ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r4.claim: This reciprocal verb can forbid one side by saying لا يجادلنك فلان, equivalent to لا تجادلنه, because argument requires two participants.
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r4.anchor: وهذا جائز في الفعل الذي لا يكون إلا من اثنين لأن المجادلة والمخاصمة لا تتم إلا باثنين

ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r5.claim: The same construction does not work with a nonreciprocal verb: لا يضربنك فلان cannot mean that you must not strike him; reciprocal لا يضاربنك can.
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r5.anchor: لا يضربنك فلان، وأنت تريد لا تضربه

ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r6.claim: A variant فلا ينزعنك means do not let them overpower you in the dispute.
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r6.anchor: معناه لا يغلبنك في المنازعة فيه

ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p437/r7.claim: Zajjaj illustrates the verb with expressions for contending and defeating an opponent: نازعني فنزعته and عازني فعززته.

ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n82/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n82/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n82/r1.claim: Mansak means a way of worship and can also denote an act of worship.
ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n82/r1.anchor: Lit., "a way of worship" (mansak, which sometimes denotes also "an act of worship").

ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n82/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n82/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n82/r2.claim: For the fuller explanation, Asad points to the second paragraph of 5:48 and its notes 66–68.
ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n82/r2.anchor: For a fuller emplanation of this passage, see the second paragraph of 5:48 - "Unto every one of you have We appointed a [different] law and way of life" - and the corresponding notes 66-68.

ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n83/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n83/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari and Baghawi
ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n83/r1.claim: Zamakhshari and Baghawi understand the instruction as not allowing oneself to be drawn into disputes.
ASAD-NOTES:22:67#n83/r1.anchor: I.e., do not allow thyself to be drawn into disputes" (Zamakhshari and Baghawi).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p221/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p221/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p221/r7.claim: The Prophet is told to leave the enemies’ matter to God and ignore their persistent misconduct, since God will soon decide their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p221/r7.anchor: he should consign their matter to God and ignore them. Soon the day will come when God decides their fate.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r3.claim: Mansak, discussed at 22:34, means a community’s ways of worship, the outward form of divine law, and its principles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r3.anchor: Here it is used for ways of worship, the apparent form of divine law and its principles

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r4.claim: Islahi says Jews and Christians were siding openly with Quraysh and fueling the debate; the verse says each community has a prescribed law, which it should follow and accept when God changes it, thereby distinguishing the sincere.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r4.anchor: it was they who were actually fuelling the whole debate. For this reason, the verse refers to them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r5.claim: Across successive messengers, changes to outward law reform innovators’ fabrications; sincere truth-seekers accept reform, while traditionalists cling to inherited views and debate against it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r5.anchor: Those who were seekers of the truth, accepted this reform with full sincerity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r6.claim: The Prophet’s opponents cling prejudicially to jāhiliyyah customs, so he should not be troubled by them or give them an opening for polemical debate; he should remain on the straight path and invite them, then leave them to themselves if they refuse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r6.anchor: he should not give them any opportunity to engage in polemical debates with him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r7.claim: The verse is compared with 2:148, where each community has a direction and people are urged to excel in good deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p228/r7.anchor: And for each there is a fixed a direction towards which it turns

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r6.claim: The verse is also compared with 5:48, which says each community has an ordained rule and path and urges people to excel in good deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r6.anchor: For each of you, We have ordained a rule and path.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r7.speaker: some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r7.claim: Some people read the cited passages as expressing tolerance toward Jews and Christians; Islahi rejects that reading and says they express aversion toward them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r7.anchor: these verses do not portray any tolerance for the Jews and Christians, as some people have understood

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r8.claim: Islahi’s preferred interpretation is that the cited verses express aversion toward Jews and Christians.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p229/r8.anchor: They actually express and declare aversion against them

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p85/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p85/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p85/r1.claim: The reading فلا ينزعنك means: remain firm in your religion and do not let desire draw you toward another faith; Ibn Jinnī connects ينزع to selecting people by belief and knowledge, not physically pulling them away.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p85/r1.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: ظاهر هذا فلا يستخفنك عن دينك إلى أديانهم، فيكون بصورة المنزوع عن شيء إلى غيره.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p85/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p85/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p85/r2.claim: The common فلا ينازعنّك tells the Prophet to remain certain and ignore their false claims; its wording forbids others to dispute him, as in لا أرينك and al-Nābigha’s verse.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p85/r2.anchor: وأما قراءة العامة: {فلا ينازعنّك في الأمر} أي: فاثبت على يقينك في صحة دينك ولا تلتفت إلى فساد أقوالهم،

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r1.claim: Fatḥa follows the verb's pattern for a verbal noun or place name; kasra derives it from the place where a sacrificial sheep is slaughtered.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p253#2/r1.anchor: يقرأ بفتح السين وكسرها فالحجة لمن فتح أنه أتى بالكلمة على أصلها وما أوجبه القياس لها لأن وجه فعل يفعل

QIRAAT-ER:22:67:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:22:67:5#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:22:67:5#1/r1.claim: Kasra on sīn yields mansikan, an alternative canonical form of the noun of place or time.
QIRAAT-ER:22:67:5#1/r1.anchor: Vowel variant: kasra on sīn instead of fatḥa — mansikan as alternative form of the noun of place/time

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p41#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p41#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p41#2/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses the rite as sacrifice and pilgrimage.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p41#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولكل أمة جعلنا منسكا ﴾ قال ذبحا وحجا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p41#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p41#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p41#2/r2.claim: Qatāda explains the command as telling others not to contend with the Prophet about the matter.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p41#2/r2.anchor: قال ﴿ فلا ينازعنك في الأمر ﴾ فلا يعالجنك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r13.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r13.claim: A reported occasion is a dispute about sacrificial meat: polytheists including Budayl ibn Warqāʾ and Bishr ibn Sufyān challenged Muslims for eating animals they slaughtered but not those God killed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r13.anchor: روي أنها نزلت بسبب جدال الكفار بديل بن ورقاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r14.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says “they perform it” shows mansak is a verbal noun, since a place noun would require “in it”; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the necessity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عطية هم ناسكوه يعطي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r15.claim: An active participle can take a locative complement directly by extension, just as a verb can; the place is treated like a direct object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p533/r15.anchor: ولا يتعين ما قال إذ قد يتسع في معمول اسم الفاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r1.claim: The cited anonymous poem uses مشرب for a drinking place and attaches a pronoun directly; its underlying sense is “I drink in it.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r1.anchor: ومشرب أشربه رسيل ... لا آجن الماء ولا وبيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r2.claim: Travel over two farsakhs is another extension in a locative expression.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r3.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r3.claim: A reading with a light nūn tells the Prophet to remain firm in his religion so opponents cannot draw him into theirs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r3.anchor: أي اثبت على دينك ثباتا لا يطمعون أن يجذبوك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r4.claim: The prohibition is rhetorically directed at opponents, like “do not let me see you here,” though their dispute will try to provoke the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r4.anchor: وهذا النهي لهم عن المنازعة من باب لا أرينك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r5.speaker: أبو مجلز
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r5.claim: Abū Mujliz reads the verb from نزع, “to pull away,” meaning they must not uproot the Prophet from his religion and carry him to theirs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز فلا ينازعنك من النزع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r6.claim: Al-amr means the religion and message brought by the Prophet; given the reported occasion, it can instead mean the slaughtering dispute.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r6.anchor: وعلى ما روي في سبب النزول يكون في الأمر بمعنى في الذبح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r7.claim: Hudā here means guidance or right direction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r7.anchor: هدى أي إرشاد. وجاء ولكل أمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p534/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says 22:34 has a conjunction because it follows related verses about sacrificial rites, while this verse lacks one because its context is semantically distant.

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r1.claim: Mansak means a distinct religious law assigned to each community; fronting “for every community” restricts each one to its own prescribed law.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r1.anchor: جعلنا ( وضعنا وعينا ( منسكا ( أي شريعة خاصة وتقديم الجار والمجرور على الفعل للقصر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r2.claim: The wording is like assigning each of four named women a different garment: no community shares or independently crosses into another's assigned law.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r2.anchor: وحاصل المعنى هنا عينا كل شريعة لأمة معينة من الأمم بحيث لا تتخطى أمة منهم شريعتها المعينة لها إلى شريعة أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r3.claim: The clause is an adjective reinforcing the restriction: each specifically designated community practices its own law, not another's.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r3.anchor: صفة لمنسكا مؤكدة للقصر والضمير لكل أمة باعتبار خصوصها أي تلك الأمة المعينة ناسكون به

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r4.claim: The community from Moses to Jesus followed the Torah, the community from Jesus to Muhammad the Gospel, and the community beginning with Muhammad follows only the Qurʾān until the end of time.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r4.anchor: الأمة التي كانت من مبعث موسى إلى مبعث عيسى عليهما السلام منسكهم ما في التوراة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r5.claim: The conclusion is that the People of Scripture must not dispute the Prophet's religion by claiming their ancestors' Torah or Gospel remains binding after its abrogation.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r5.anchor: موجب لطاعة هؤلاء له صلى الله عليه وسلم وعدم منازعتهم إياه في أمر الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r6.claim: The apparent reading is a real prohibition directed at them; the alternative makes it an indirect instruction for the Prophet to ignore their dispute, which better suits the next command but departs from the apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r6.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد نهيهم حقيقة عن النزاع في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r7.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes the prohibition as a metonymic command to the Prophet not to dispute with them, as in “do not let Zayd fight you,” though the author questions the analogy for reciprocal verbs.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r7.anchor: هو نهي له عليه الصلاة والسلام على منازعتهم كما تقول : لا يضاربنك زيد

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r8.claim: A variant reads the verb with a light nūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r8.anchor: فلا ينازعنك ) بالنون الخفيفة وقرأ أبو مجلز

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r9.speaker: أبو مجلز ولاحق بن حميد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r9.claim: Abū Majliz and Lāḥiq ibn Ḥumayd read “fa-lā yanziʿannaka,” with kasra on zāy, from the verb meaning to pull or draw away.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز ولاحق بن حميد ( فلا ينزعنك ) بكسر الزاي على أنه من النزع

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r10.speaker: ابن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r10.claim: Ibn Jinnī explains the variant as “do not let them pull you from your religion to theirs,” so you seem uprooted from one position to another.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195/r10.anchor: كما قال ابن جني فلا يستخفنك عن دينك إلى أديانهم فتكون بصورة المنزوع عن شيء إلى غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r1.claim: The author explains that this intensifies the Prophet's firmness by stirring his zeal and anger for God and His religion, a device common in the Qurʾān.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r1.anchor: التثبيت له عليه الصلاة والسلام بما يهيج حميته ويلهب غضبه لله تعالى ولدينه ومثله كثير في القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the command urges the Prophet to stand firm so they cannot pull him away, stirring his zeal and anger for God and His religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r2.anchor: التثبيت له عليه الصلاة والسلام بما يهيج حميته ويلهب غضبه لله تعالى ولدينه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj derives the expression from mutual disputation followed by one party prevailing: “do not let them defeat you in argument.”
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج : هو من نازعته فنزعته أنزعه أي غلبته فالمعنى لا يغلبنك في المنازعة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r4.claim: For most grammarians, the prevailing form in this verb class takes ḍamma on the second radical; the claimed guttural exception is rejected by scholars, making al-Zajjāj's analysis irregular.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r4.anchor: عند الجمهور تقال في كل فعل فاعلته ففعلته أفعله بصم العين ولا تكسر إلا شذوذا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r5.claim: Sībawayh notes that the “prevail over one another” pattern does not apply to every verb; here “overcome” is the ordinary alternative.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r5.anchor: وقال سيبويه : كما في المفصل وليس في كل شيء يكون هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r6.claim: On al-Zajjāj's analysis, the force is not to refrain from an action but to keep debating without falling short until the opponents prevail, intensifying the Prophet's resolve.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r6.anchor: لا تقصر في منازعتهم حتى يغلبوك فيها وفيه مبالغة في التثبيت

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r7.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r7.claim: ʿAṭāʾ's report from Ibn ʿAbbās takes mansak to mean a religious law; al-Qaffāl chose this, and al-Imām calls it the closest view.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r7.anchor: وما ذكرنا من تفسير المنسك بالشريعة هو رواية عطاء عن ابن عباس واختاره القفال

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r8.claim: Another view takes mansak as a verbal noun meaning worship or ritual; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says “they perform it” supports that reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : هو مصدر بمعنى النسك أي العبادة قال ابن عطية : يعطي ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r9.claim: Other lexical proposals take mansak as a time or a place; for the place sense one might expect “performing it there,” though the expression is extended.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r9.anchor: وقيل : هو اسم زمان وقيل : اسم مكان وكان الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r10.claim: Mujāhid says mansak means slaughter or sacrifice.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد : هو الذبح + وأخرج ذلك الحاكم وصححه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r11.speaker: الحاكم عن علي بن الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḥākim and al-Bayhaqī transmit the slaughter gloss from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn; al-Ḥākim grades his report sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r11.anchor: وأخرج ذلك الحاكم وصححه والبيهقي عن علي بن الحسن رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that mansak means slaughter.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r12.anchor: وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وعبد بن حميد عن عكرمة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r13.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r13.claim: ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd transmits from ʿIkrima that mansak means slaughter.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r13.anchor: وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وعبد بن حميد عن عكرمة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r14.claim: One occasion-of-revelation account says the disputants were idolaters and the subject was sacrifice: Khuzāʿī leaders asked why believers ate what they slaughtered but not what God slaughtered.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r14.anchor: لما ذكر من أن الآية نزلت بسبب قول الخزاعيين بديل بن ورقاء وبشر بن سفيان ويزيد بن خنيس

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r15.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r15.claim: Shaykh al-Islām rejects limiting the dispute to sacrifices, since it would make carrion and other pagan falsehoods divinely assigned rites; the answer is that God assigned each nation its own rites, not the pagans' practices.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r15.anchor: وتعقبه شيخ الإسلام بأنه مما لا سبيل إليه أصلا كيف لا وأنه يستدعي أن يكون أكل الميتة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r16.claim: A further explanation says not to heed the pagan dispute about slaughter: sacrifice is an ancient rite prescribed for communities, not exclusive to Muhammad's community.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r16.anchor: لا تلتفت إلى نزاع المشركين في أمر الذبائح فإنا جعلنا لكل أمة من أهل الأديان ذبحاهم ذابحوه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r17.claim: For those who accept the transmitted reports, the sacrifice interpretation best explains the verse; without that commitment, the author favors the broader law-for-each-community reading already given.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r17.anchor: ومن قال بصحة الآثار وعص عليها بالنواجذ لا يكاد يجد أولى منه بيان حاصل الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r18.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r18.claim: Al-Kashf says the preceding rites and benefits strongly connect to “for every community We appointed a rite,” echoing the pilgrims' benefits and remembrance and showing the rite is ancient and beneficial in both worlds.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r18.anchor: أي في الشعائر منافع دينية ودنيوية كوجوب نحرها منتهية إلى البيت العتيق كالإعادة لما في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r19.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r19.claim: Al-Ṭībī links the statement to the command to honor God's rites and says this worship is not exclusive to Muslims, since every community has its own rite.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p195#2/r19.anchor: ما تقدم عطف على قوله تعالى ( ومن يعظم شعائر الله ) الخ وهو من تتمة الكلام مع المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r1.claim: The verse prepares the command not to dispute, consoles and honors the Prophet, and teaches prophets to leave ignorant disputants alone while continuing to call to monotheism.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r1.anchor: وهذه الآية مقدمة نهي النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عما يوجب نزاع القوم تسلية له وتعظيم لأمره

ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r2.claim: Alternatively, every obstinate earlier nation had a path and religion it followed; calling its persistent practice a rite is ironic and consoles the Messenger.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r2.anchor: أو لكل أمة من الأمم الخالية المعاندة جعلنا طريقا ودينا هم ناسكوه فلا ينازعنك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r3.claim: One coherence proposal links this to the disbelievers' continuing doubt (22:55): intervening verses console the Prophet, so he should emulate earlier prophets by ending debate after despair of their faith, with God's judgment (22:69) as support.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r3.anchor: فإن قوله تعالى ( ولا يزال الذين كفروا في مرية منه ) يوجب القلع عن إنذار القوم والإياس منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r4.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r4.claim: Al-Kashf objects that the intervening passage about recompense (22:60) cannot reinforce consolation, especially on the view that it concerns fighting in the sacred month; if it could, the independent clause would still set up the prohibition that follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r4.anchor: تعقب في الكشف اتصاله بما ذكر بأنه لا وجه له فقد تخلل ما لا يصلح لتأكيد معنى التسلية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r5.claim: Al-Alūsī calls the consolation linkage far-fetched and says the sūra's central theme is disputation with obstinate opponents, opened and repeatedly signaled by 22:3; that theme supports the verse's placement.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r5.anchor: والذي يدور عليه قطب هذه السورة الكريمة الكلام في مجادلة القوم ومعانديهم والنعي عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r6.claim: “Call” addresses the disputants or all people, with the disputants included first; it means inviting them to God's oneness and worship according to the prescribed law.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r6.anchor: وادع أي وادع هؤلاء المنازعين أو الناس كافة على أنهم داخلون فيهم دخولا أوليا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r7.claim: Guidance is pictured as a straight path leading to truth; the path metaphor may refer either to the religion and law or to their proofs.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197/r7.anchor: طريق موصل إلى الحق ففيه استعارة مكنية

ALUSI-FULL:v17p197#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197#2/r1.claim: In the path metaphor, one of “straight” and “upon” may be imaginative and the other a reinforcing metaphorical extension; the sentence is an explanatory resumption giving the reason for the command.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p197#2/r1.anchor: أي سوى أو أحدهما تخييل والآخر ترشيح ثم المراد بهذا الطريق إما الدين والشريعة أو أدلتها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains mansakan as a religious law practiced by each community.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني شريعة هم عاملون بها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r11.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās gives “festival” as another meaning of mansak.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r11.anchor: وروي عنه أنه قال: عيدا قال قتادة ومجاهد: موضع قربان يذبحون فيه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r12.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r12.claim: Qatādah and Mujāhid understand it as a place where sacrificial offerings are slaughtered.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r12.anchor: قال قتادة ومجاهد: موضع قربان يذبحون فيه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r13.claim: Other views take mansak as a place of worship or a familiar place people frequent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r13.anchor: وقيل: موضع عبادة. وقيل: مألفا يألفونه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r14.claim: In Arabic, mansak is a customary place for a good or bad act; pilgrimage rites are called manāsik because people repeatedly visit their sites.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398/r14.anchor: المنسك في كلام العرب: الموضع المعتاد لعمل خير أو شر، ومنه "مناسك الحج" لتردد الناس إلى أماكن أعمال الحج.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r1.claim: The matter in which they dispute is the rules for sacrificial animals.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r1.anchor: {فلا ينازعنك في الأمر} يعني في أمر الذبائح. نزلت في بديل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r2.claim: The verse was revealed about Budayl ibn Warqāʾ, Bishr ibn Sufyān, and Yazīd ibn Khunays, who challenged the Companions’ distinction between animals people killed and those God killed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r2.anchor: نزلت في بديل بن ورقاء، وبشر بن سفيان، ويزيد بن خنيس قالوا لأصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the form as “do not dispute with them”; reciprocal dispute ceases when one side stops, unlike a one-sided act such as striking.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: معنى قوله {فلا ينازعنك} أي: لا تنازعهم أنت، كما يقال: لا يخاصمك فلان،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r4.claim: Call people to belief in your Lord.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r5.claim: The Prophet is upon straight guidance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p398#2/r5.anchor: وادع إلى ربك} إلى الإيمان بربك، {إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم}

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r1.claim: An umma here means a community belonging to a religion.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r2.claim: Mansak may mean a place of worship, a revealed law or ritual practice, or a festival.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r2.anchor: جعلنا منسكا } متعبدا أو شريعة تعبدوا بها، وقيل عيدا.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r3.claim: They are the ones who perform the worship or practice.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r3.anchor: منسكا } متعبدا أو شريعة تعبدوا بها، وقيل عيدا. { هم ناسكوه

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r4.speaker: author
