BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r4.claim: Adherents of other religions should not draw the Prophet into dispute about religion or rites: they are ignorant or obstinate, and his religion is too clear to be disputed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r4.anchor: فلا ينزعنك } سائر أرباب الملل. { في الأمر } في أمر الدين أو النسائك لأنهم بين جهال

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r5.claim: Another explanation is that the Prophet must not attend to their words or let them draw him into debate, since debate benefits truth-seekers whereas they are contentious.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد نهي الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الالتفات إلى قولهم وتمكينهم من المناظرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r6.claim: Alternatively, it means “do not contend with them,” like lā yuḍārru bika Zayd; this usage is limited to intensive reciprocal verbs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r6.anchor: أو عن منازعتهم كقولك: لا يضار بك زيد، وهذا إنما يجوز في أفعال المبالغة للتلازم

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r7.claim: The verse is also said to have been revealed about Khuzāʿa, who asked Muslims why they ate what they killed but not what God killed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r7.anchor: وقيل نزلت في كفار خزاعة قالوا للمسلمين: ما لكم تأكلون ما قتلتم ولا تأكلون

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r8.claim: A reading here exhorts the Prophet and intensifies his firmness in religion, from an expression for overcoming someone in dispute.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r8.anchor: وقرىء { فلا ينزعنك } على تهييج الرسول والمبالغة في تثبيته على دينه

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r9.claim: Calling to the Lord means calling to His oneness and worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r9.anchor: وادع إلى ربك } إلى توحيده وعبادته.

BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r10.claim: The straight guidance is an even path leading to the truth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:22:67/r10.anchor: إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم } طريق إلى الحق سوي.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r1.claim: The preceding evidence from 2:106 establishes that disputing God's ruling is unbelief; this verse follows without a conjunction because the connection is complete.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r1.anchor: فعلم أن منازعتهم فيه كفر , فلذلك أتبع هذا قوله من غير عاطف لما بينهما من تمام الاتصال

BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r2.claim: For every community in every age God prescribed a rite or law through which they gather around their Creator in obedience, or gather around their own desires when it opposes His command.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r2.anchor: لكل أمة } أي في كل زمان { جعلنا } أي بما لنا من العظمة { منسكا } أي شرعا لاجتماعهم به على خالقهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir says the basic Arabic meaning of mansak is a place a person regularly visits, for good or ill.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r3.anchor: وعن ابن جرير أم أصل المنسك في كلام العرب هو الموضع الذي يعتاده الإنسان

BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r4.claim: They will perform the prescribed rite; God defends them against its opponents until the matter is established, whether for their felicity or misery.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r4.anchor: هم ناسكوه } أي متعبدون به , لأنا ندافع عنهم من يعاديهم فيه حتى يستقيم لهم أمره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r5.claim: Doubting God's ability to establish the rite is unbelief; obeying it brings faith and gain, while opposing it brings unbelief and loss.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r5.anchor: فمن شك في قدرتنا على تمكينهم منه فهو كفور , فإن وافق الأمر كان ربحا وإيمانا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r6.claim: The Prophet should not heed disputes raised through satanic doubts about his religion, including objections that abrogation would imply a change of knowledge or badāʾ in God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r6.anchor: بما يلقيه الشيطان إليهم من الشبه ليجادلوا به , من طعنهم في دينك بالنسخ بقولهم : لو كان من عند الله لما أمر اليوم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r7.claim: The author rejects the claim that abrogation implies badāʾ: it instead shows God's foreknowledge of outcomes and complete power to legislate.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r7.anchor: فليس الأمر كما زعموا , بل هو دال على العم بالعواقب والاقتدار التام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r8.claim: The verse is reported to have been revealed after pagans, including Budayl b. Waraqāʾ and Bishr b. Sufyān al-Khuzāʿī, argued over slaughter: Muslims ate animals they killed but not those killed by God, meaning carrion.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r8.anchor: وروي أنها نزلت بسبب جدال الكفار بديل بن ورقاء وبشر بن سفيان الخزاعين وغيرهما في الذبائح

BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r9.claim: He is to call all people to his Lord and carry out each command without fear or calculation of consequences; arranging the eventual success of the religion belongs to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r9.anchor: وكان التعبير بما تقدم من تحويله إليهم لتأكيد الأمر مع دلالته على إجلاله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r10.claim: The Prophet is firmly on straight guidance because it comes from the All-Knowing, Almighty, even if its course appears to change.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p173/r10.anchor: فإنه تأصيل العليم القدير وإن طرقه التغيير

DURR-FULL:v6p72/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r3.speaker: أبو المليح
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r3.claim: Abu al-Malih defines an ummah as a group of forty to a hundred or more.
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r3.anchor: عن أبي المليح قال: الأمة ما بين الأربعين إلى المائة فصاعدا

DURR-FULL:v6p72/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r4.speaker: علي بن الحسين
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r4.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn glosses the ritual as a sacrifice that the community performs.
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r4.anchor: عن علي بن الحسين {لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا هم ناسكوه} قال: ذبحا هم ذابحوه

DURR-FULL:v6p72/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r5.claim: Abu Rafi reports the Prophet sacrificed two rams: one for his monotheist community and one for himself and his family, fed the poor, ate with his household, and Banu Hashim abstained two years as costs were covered.
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r5.anchor: حدثني أبو رافع أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان إذا ضحى: اشترى كبشين سمينين أملحين أقرنين

DURR-FULL:v6p72/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the community is sacrificing, and the command not to dispute concerns the sacrifices.
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {هم ناسكوه} يعني هم ذابحوه {فلا ينازعنك في الأمر} يعني في أمر الذبائح

DURR-FULL:v6p72/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r7.claim: Ikrima glosses the ritual as a sacrifice.
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه {لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا هم ناسكوه} قال ذبحا هم ذابحوه

DURR-FULL:v6p72/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r8.claim: Mujahid glosses the ritual as shedding the blood of the sacrificial offering.
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {منسكا هم ناسكوه} قال: اهراقه دم الهدي

DURR-FULL:v6p72/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r9.claim: Qatada says the rite comprises sacrifice and pilgrimage.
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r9.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا} قال: ذبحا وحجا

DURR-FULL:v6p72/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r10.claim: Mujahid reports the polytheists' challenge: they reject what God slaughtered while accepting what people slaughtered themselves.
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {فلا ينازعنك في الأمر} قول أهل الشرك أما ما ذبح الله بيمينه فلا تأكلون

DURR-FULL:v6p72/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r11.speaker: مقاتل
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r11.claim: Muqatil glosses the call as inviting people to the Lord's religion and the straight guidance as the upright religion.
DURR-FULL:v6p72/r11.anchor: عن مقاتل رضي الله عنه {وادع إلى ربك} قال: إلى دين ربك {إنك لعلى هدى} قال: دين مستقيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r1.claim: This verse resumes the subject of the ritual appointed for every community in verse 34 after the intervening discussion of divine defense and the believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r1.anchor: هذا متصل في المعنى بقوله : { ولكل أمة جعلنا منسكا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r2.claim: Earlier communities each received one rite of approach to the one God, supporting monotheism; polytheists instead multiplied sacrificial sites, with a separate shrine for each idol.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r2.anchor: بأن الله ما جعل لأهل كل ملة سبقت إلا منسكا واحدا يتقربون فيه إلى الله لأن المتقرب إليه واحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r3.speaker: النابغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r3.claim: Al-Nābigha’s line uses jasad for blood poured over idols, illustrating the sacrifices made at polytheist shrines.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r3.anchor: قال النابغة : وما هريق على الأنصاب من جسد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r4.claim: The sentence begins anew, rather than being conjoined, because its relation to the earlier ritual statement is already clear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r4.anchor: فالجملة استئناف . والمناسبة ظاهرة ولذلك فصلت الجملة ولم تعطف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r5.claim: With fatḥ on both mīm and sīn, mansak is a place of ritual; here it means pilgrimage sites, whereas verse 34 means a place of sacrifice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r5.anchor: والمنسك بفتح الميم وفتح السين : اسم مكان النسك بضمهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r6.claim: The pronoun in nāsikūhu is accusative through omission of a preposition: they perform the rite in that place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r6.anchor: والضمير في { ناسكوه } منصوب على نزع الخافض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r7.claim: The Muwatta reports that Quraysh stood at Qazah in Muzdalifah while other Arabs stood at Arafah, each claiming the superior station; the report says this dispute occasioned the verse and cites people of knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p327/r7.anchor: وفي ( الموطأ ) : ( أن قريشا كانت تقف عند المشعر الحرام بالمزدلفة بقزح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r1.speaker: الباجي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r1.claim: Al-Baji, following Rabiʿa, says the verse came after pilgrimage became obligatory for Muslims but before polytheists were barred, which would date it to year nine; Ibn Ashur says the stronger view is otherwise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r1.anchor: قال الباجي في ( المنتقى ) : ( وهو قول ربيعة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r2.claim: The prohibition appears addressed to the Prophet, but targets opponents: he must leave them no basis for dispute, an indirect prohibition of the listener’s causes modeled on the Arab idiom do not let me find you doing this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r2.anchor: فالنهي ظاهره موجه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن ما أعطيه من الحجج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes the prohibition as directed to the Messenger: because mutual-action wording can involve either party, forbidding his dispute also prevents the opponents’ counter-dispute; the result is to avoid debating them after the proofs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج : هو نهي للرسول عن منازعتهم لأن صيغة المفاعلة تقتضي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r4.claim: The otherwise unspecified matter means monotheism, as the surrounding evidence indicates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r4.anchor: واسم { الأمر } هنا مجمل مراد به التوحيد بالقرينة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r5.claim: Polytheists may have claimed their Abrahamic religion was true because the Prophet affirmed pilgrimage; the verse answers that pilgrimage is a true monotheistic rite, while other rites are later falsehoods.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r5.anchor: فكان قوله تعالى : { لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا هم ناسكوه } كشفا لشبهتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r6.claim: The polytheist reading best fits the recurring pronouns through verse 72 and the surah’s mixed late-Meccan and early-Medinan setting; a dispute with the People of the Book is less likely.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p328/r6.anchor: وهذا المحمل هو المناسب لتناسق الضمائر العائدة على المشركين مما تقدم إلى قوله { وعدها الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r1.claim: After ending the dispute, the Prophet is told to continue calling people rather than stop once proof has prevailed, since stubbornness resists persuasion and continued preaching benefits everyone; the omitted object makes the call general.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r1.anchor: عطف على انتهاء المنازعة في الدين أمر بالدوام على الدعوة وعدم الاكتفاء بظهور الحجة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r2.claim: The statement that the Prophet is on straight guidance explains why he should persist in calling; it functions as a causal explanation, not as a reply to doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r2.anchor: وجملة { إنك لعلى هدى مستقيم } تعليل للدوام على الدعوة وأنها قائمة مقام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r3.claim: The preposition ʿalā is metaphorical, portraying the Prophet as firmly established upon guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r3.anchor: و { على } مستعارة للتمكن من الهدى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r4.claim: Guidance is implicitly likened to a road leading to its destination; calling it straight signals swift arrival, and Islam is the easiest path to spiritual perfection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r4.anchor: شبه الهدى بالطريق الموصل إلى المطلوب ورمز إليه بالمستقيم لأن المستقيم أسرع إيصالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r5.claim: This assurance strengthens the Prophet and renews his resolve to carry the burdens of the call.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p329/r5.anchor: وفي هذا الخبر تثبيت للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم وتجديد لنشاطه في الاضطلاع بأعباء الدعوة

MALIK:874/r1.author: MALIK
MALIK:874/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
MALIK:874/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says all of Arafat is a standing place except Urana valley, and all of Muzdalifah except Muhassir valley.
MALIK:874/r1.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة، عن عبد الله بن الزبير، أنه كان يقول

MALIK:874/r4.author: MALIK
MALIK:874/r4.speaker: author
MALIK:874/r4.claim: Malik says jidal in pilgrimage was the dispute between Quraysh at Muzdalifah and others at Arafat over whose rite was correct, answered by 22:67's command not to contest the matter.
MALIK:874/r4.anchor: فكانوا يتجادلون يقول هؤلاء نحن أصوب ويقول هؤلاء نحن أصوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r2.claim: Mansak can be the verbal noun for worship or religious law, and also the place where a rite is performed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r2.anchor: المصدر فهو بمعنى العبادة والشرعة، وهو أيضا موضع النسك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r3.claim: One group reads the sin of mansak with fatḥa and another with kasra; Ibn Atiyya says the issue was treated earlier in this sura.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r3.anchor: وقرأت فرقة بفتح السين وفرقة بكسرها وقد تقدم القول فيه في هذه السورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r4.claim: The phrase هم ناسكوه supports taking mansak as an action or verbal noun: if it meant a place, the wording would be هم ناسكون فيه.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r4.anchor: وقوله هم ناسكوه يعطي أن المنسك المصدر ولو كان الموضع لقيل هم ناسكون فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r5.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r5.claim: A group says the verse was revealed when unbelievers argued over sacrifice, claiming believers ate what they slaughtered but not what God killed as carrion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r5.anchor: وروت فرقة أن هذه الآية نزلت بسبب جدال الكفار في أمر الذبائح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r6.claim: The prohibition may threaten the disputants or belittle them as too insignificant to engage; Ibn Atiyya prefers the latter sense here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r6.anchor: تحتمل معنى التخويف، وتحتمل معنى احتقار الفاعل وأنه أقل من أن يفاعل وهذا هو المعنى في هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq explains it as do not argue with them lest they argue with you, an interpretation suited to the threatening sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: المعنى فلا تنازعهم فينازعوك ع وهذا التقدير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya explains the prohibition as an implied statement that they have no power to dispute with the Prophet, like لا أرينك meaning do not be here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r8.anchor: فلا يد لهم بمنازعتك، فالنهي إنما يراد به معنى من غير اللفظ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r9.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «فلا ينزعنك» ، وقوله في الأمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r10.claim: If mansak means religious law, the affair is religion or scripture; if it means a sacrificial site, the matter is slaughter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r10.anchor: معناه على التأويل أن المنسك الشرعة لا ينازعنك في الدين والكتاب ونحوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p132#2/r11.anchor: و «الهدى» في هذه الآية الإرشاد، وقوله وإن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r1.claim: The term mansakan was explained earlier in this sūra at 22:34.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r1.anchor: قد سبق بيانه في هذه السورة الحج 34

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r2.claim: Quraysh and Khuzāʿa disputed Muhammad over sacrificial slaughter, asking why Muslims ate what they killed but not what God killed (carrion).
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r2.anchor: وذلك ان كفار قريش وخزاعة خاصموا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في أمر الذبيحة فقالوا كيف تأكلون ما قتلتم ولا تأكلون ما قتله الله يعنون الميتة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the prohibition is addressed to Muhammad: do not dispute with them. A reciprocal verb can be phrased as “so-and-so should not dispute with you”; the following “if they dispute” confirms this sense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r3.anchor: المراد النهي له عن منازعتهم فالمعنى لا تنازعنهم كما تقول للرجل لا يخاصمنك فلان في هذا أبدا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the reciprocal construction is permitted with disputing, which requires two parties, but not with a one-way verb such as “strike”; “do not exchange blows” works like “do not dispute.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r4.anchor: وهذا جائز في الفعل الذي لا يكون الا من اثنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r5.claim: The call is to God's religion and belief in Him; their argument concerns sacrificial meat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p448#3/r5.anchor: وادع إلى ربك أي إلى دينه والإيمان به وجادلوك بمعنى خاصموك في أمر الذبائح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r1.claim: God appointed a rite for every community.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى أنه جعل لكل قوم (2) منسكا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r2.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jarir says each community had a prophet with a rite.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن جرير: يعني: لكل أمة نبي منسكا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jarir explains the Arabic root as a place a person habitually visits for good or ill; hajj rites are called manāsik because people repeatedly attend them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r3.anchor: وأصل المنسك في كلام العرب: هو الموضع الذي يعتاده الإنسان، ويتردد إليه، إما لخير أو شر. قال: ولهذا سميت مناسك الحج بذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r4.claim: If Ibn Jarir's interpretation is intended, the command not to dispute refers to the polytheists.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r4.anchor: فإن كان كما قال من أن المراد: {لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا} فيكون المراد بقوله: {فلا ينازعنك في الأمر} أي: هؤلاء المشركون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, if every community was given its rite by God's decree, as in 2:148, they perform it by God's will; their dispute should neither trouble the Prophet nor divert him from the truth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r5.anchor: كما قال: {ولكل وجهة هو موليها} [البقرة: 148] ولهذا قال هاهنا: {هم ناسكوه} أي: فاعلوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r6.claim: The Prophet is to continue calling to his Lord because he is on a clear, straight path that leads to the goal.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r6.anchor: أي: طريق واضح مستقيم موصل إلى المقصود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir links the command to call to one's Lord with the command not to let opponents divert the Prophet from God's revealed signs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p451#2/r7.anchor: وهذه كقوله: {ولا يصدنك عن آيات الله بعد إذ أنزلت إليك وادع إلى ربك}

JISHUMI:v7p5000/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r7.claim: Mansak means a customary place for good or evil, a place to which one becomes accustomed.
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r7.anchor: والمنسك: أصله الموضع المعتاد لعمل خير أو شر، وهو المألف لذلك، والمنسك: المكان تألفه

JISHUMI:v7p5000/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r8.claim: Nusuk with ḍamma means worship, a nāsik is a worshipper, nasīka is an offering, and mansak its sacrificial place.
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r8.anchor: والنسك بضم النون: العبادة، والناسك: العابد، والنسيكة: الذبيحة، والمنسك: الموضع تذبح فيه النسائك

JISHUMI:v7p5000/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r9.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r9.claim: The poetic line uses نسك in describing a place or station.

JISHUMI:v7p5000/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r10.claim: The word المنسك has two vocalizations: fatḥa or kasra on its second syllable.

JISHUMI:v7p5000/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r12.speaker: يزيد بن ورقاء وجماعة
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r12.claim: The verse is said to have been revealed after Yazid ibn Waraqah and others asked why Muslims ate animals they killed but not those killed by God.
JISHUMI:v7p5000/r12.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (لكل أمة) في يزيد بن ورقاء وجماعة، قالوا لأصحاب رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: ما بالكم تأكلون ما تقتلون بأيديكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r1.claim: He interprets mansak as a festival.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنه العيد , قاله ابن قتيبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r2.claim: Mansak means the customary sites for the rites of Hajj and ʿumra.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنها المواضع المعتادة لمناسك الحج والعمرة , قاله الفراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r3.claim: Mansak means the place of sacrifice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r3.anchor: الثالث : المذبح , قاله الضحاك . الرابع : المنسك

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r4.claim: Mansak is worship and nusuk is worship; a worshipper is therefore called a nasik.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p38#2/r4.anchor: الرابع : المنسك المتعبد والنسك العبادة ومنه سمي العابد ناسكا , قاله الحسن

MUQATIL:22:67/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:67/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:67/r1.claim: For earlier peoples, a “manasak” means a sacrifice involving the shedding of sacrificial blood at their festival.
MUQATIL:22:67/r1.anchor: يعنى لكل قوم فيما خلا { جعلنا منسكا } يعنى ذبحا، يعنى هراقة الدماء ذبيحة فى عيدهم

MUQATIL:22:67/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:67/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:67/r2.claim: “They perform it” means they slaughter the sacrifice; the same word “nusuk” means sacrifice in 6:162.
MUQATIL:22:67/r2.anchor: يعني ذبيحتي { فلا ينازعنك في الأمر } يعنى فى أمر الذبائح

MUQATIL:22:67/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:67/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:67/r3.claim: The dispute concerns sacrifices; Muhammad is more entitled to the matter than the unbelievers of Khuzāʿa and others.
MUQATIL:22:67/r3.anchor: يعنى فى أمر الذبائح، فإنك أولى بالأمر منهم، أي من كفار خزاعة وغيرهم

MUQATIL:22:67/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:67/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:67/r4.claim: The verse was revealed about Badil ibn Warqa, Bishr ibn Sufyan al-Khuzaʿi, and Yazid ibn al-Halbas of Banu al-Harith ibn ʿAbd Manaf.
MUQATIL:22:67/r4.anchor: نزلت فى بديل بن ورقاء الخزاعى، وبشر بن سفيان الخزاعي، ويزيد بن الحلبس، من بني الحارث بن عبد مناف

MUQATIL:22:67/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:67/r5.speaker: بديل بن ورقاء وبشر بن سفيان ويزيد بن الحلبس
MUQATIL:22:67/r5.claim: They told the Muslims that animals killed by their own hands were lawful but those killed by God—carrion—were forbidden.
MUQATIL:22:67/r5.anchor: لقولهم للمسلمين، فى الأنعام، ما قتلتم أنتم بأيديكم فهو حلال وما قتل الله فهو حرام

MUQATIL:22:67/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:22:67/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:22:67/r6.claim: The call is to know God through affirming His oneness; the Prophet follows the straight religion.
MUQATIL:22:67/r6.anchor: يعني إلى معرفة ربك وهو التوحيد { إنك لعلى هدى } يعني لعلى دين { مستقيم }

NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r1.claim: God prescribed a sacrificial rite for every religious community, refuting those who claim sacrifice is not part of God's law.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ لكل أمة ﴾ أهل دين ﴿ جعلنا منسكا ﴾ من بيانه وهو رد لقول من يقول ان الذبح ليس بشريعة الله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r2.claim: They are the ones who perform that rite.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r3.claim: Do not heed their argument or allow them to draw you into disputation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r3.anchor: فلا يجادلنك والمعنى فلا تلتفت إلى قولهم ولا تمكنهم من أن ينازعوك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r4.claim: The matter in dispute may mean the sacrificial rites or the religion.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r5.speaker: المشركون
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r5.claim: The verse was revealed when polytheists challenged Muslims for eating animals they slaughtered but not carrion they said God had killed.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r5.anchor: نزلت حين قال المشركون للمسلمين ما لكم تأكلون ما قتلتم ولا تأكلون ما قتله الله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r6.claim: The Prophet is told to call people to worship his Lord.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r6.anchor: ﴿ وادع ﴾ الناس ﴿ إلى ربك ﴾ إلى عبادة ربك

NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p112#3/r7.claim: The Prophet is on an upright path.

QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r1.claim: Mansakan means a prescribed law, and nasikuhu means those who practice it.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { لكل أمة جعلنا منسكا } أي شرعا. { هم ناسكوه } أي عاملون به

QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r2.claim: No one should dispute with the Prophet about what is prescribed for his community, since laws differed in each era.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r2.anchor: { فلا ينازعنّك في الأمر } أي لا ينازعنك أحد منهم فيما يشرع لأمتك

QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r3.speaker: فرقة
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r3.claim: One group reports that the verse answered pagans arguing that Muslims eat animals they slaughter but not carrion killed by God, claiming God's killing should be more worthy to eat.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r3.anchor: وروت فرقة أن هذه الآية نزلت بسبب جدال الكفار في أمر الذبائح

QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r4.claim: The phrase indicates that mansak is an action or verbal noun: if it meant a place, it would say they are worshippers in it.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r4.anchor: { هم ناسكوه } يعطي أن المنسك المصدر، ولو كان الموضع لقال هم ناسكون فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r5.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses the phrase as 'let them not argue with you,' supported by the following mention of their arguing.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج: «فلا ينازعنك في الأمر» أي فلا يجادلنك ودل على هذا «وإن جادلوك»

QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r6.claim: Though opponents did dispute, the reciprocal form means 'do not dispute with them yourself'; it is like telling someone not to fight back when attacked.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r6.anchor: ولا يقال: لا يضربنك زيد وأنت تريد لا تضرب زيدا

QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r7.speaker: أبو مجلز
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r7.claim: Abu Mujliz reads falā yanza'nnaka, meaning do not let them snatch or overpower you and divert you from your religion; the common reading means disputing.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو مجلز «فلا ينزعنك في الأمر» أي لا يستخفنك ولا يغلبنك عن دينك

QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r8.claim: Both readings address the unbelievers while intending the Prophet as the recipient of the warning.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r8.anchor: ولفظ النهي في القراءتين للكفار، والمراد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r9.claim: Calling to the Lord means calling people to God's oneness, religion, and faith in Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r9.anchor: { وادع إلى ربك } أي إلى توحيده ودينه والإيمان به

QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r10.claim: The Prophet is upon guidance, meaning a straight religion with no crookedness.
QURTUBI-FULL:22:67/r10.anchor: { إنك لعلى هدى } أي دين. { مستقيم } أي قويم لا اعوجاج فيه

NASHR:v2p325/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p325/r9.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
NASHR:v2p325/r9.claim: Hamza, al-Kisai, and Khalaf use kasr on the sīn in both occurrences of mansakan; the remaining readers use fatḥ.
NASHR:v2p325/r9.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف بكسر السين فيهما، وقرأ الباقون بفتحها منهما
